section_job.evidence: Lines 3-12 stay entirely within the approved job. The paragraph at line 3 argues why L&D data matters (terminal point of the IPCC risk chain + the 11/260 draft-only catalog gap); the list at lines 9-10 plus the closing paragraph at line 12 establish the two dimensions used throughout the chapter (event-timing, damage-type). No drift into MVD form/field design or quantitative valuation methodology, both of which the contract reserves for the next topic.

audience_decision_value.evidence: The line-3 paragraph foregrounds what the department/policy audience needs to understand before seeing MVD detail: why L&D data is the country's only way to verify whether assessed risk became real impact. The one process mention ('คณะที่ปรึกษาจัดทำในบทที่ 2', line 3; 'คณะที่ปรึกษาออกแบบในหัวข้อถัดไป', line 12) is a brief, necessary attribution of the 11/260 figure and the coming MVD, not workflow narration.

evidence_payload.evidence: Line 3 paragraph carries claim (L&D = risk-chain terminal point) + concrete evidence (11/260 datasets, all draft/unendorsed) + consequence (no standard/tool for real collection yet) + mechanism (chapter 3 fills this gap). Lines 9-12 carry claim (two dimensions) + concrete examples (flood/windstorm; sea-level rise/mean-temperature shift/heat-cold extremes; repair-cost-valued physical damage vs. income/output/service-loss economic loss) + consequence (mixing the two dimensions corrupts the resulting figures) + mechanism (this split structures the MVD in the next topic).

causal_logic.evidence: Line 3: risk-chain terminal point -> without this data the country cannot verify assessed risk became impact -> the catalog already reserves the domain but lacks standard/tooling -> this is chapter 3's reason to exist. Line 12: separating the two dimensions -> structures the MVD; conflating them -> resulting figures reflect neither true asset value nor economic-flow impact, named as the country's current data problem. No reversed causality, unsupported leap, or decorative transition found.

reader_facing_appropriateness.evidence: No slide/page locators anywhere in the draft. No inline arrow-chain rendering of the IPCC risk chain -- the chain's terminal-point expansion is deferred to the figure placeholder at line 5 exactly as target_altitude requires, and the placeholder text lists the four sub-categories with commas, not arrows. One minor redundant forward-reference at line 12 ('ดังจะเห็นได้ในหัวข้อถัดไป') is logged as finding F2 -- it edges toward document-structure meta-commentary but is attached to a substantive claim (the dimension-mixing problem), not a bare structural pointer, so it does not on its own fail this dimension.

terminology_agency.evidence: Uses the short form 'โครงสร้างข้อมูลฯ' per the contract's terminology note (line 3) without re-stating the full name, correctly deferring to chapter 1's first mention. 'คณะที่ปรึกษา' (the consultant) is consistently the actor for the chapter-2 catalog and the chapter-3-onward MVD design (line 3, line 12), never substituted with 'โครงการ', 'กรมฯ', or the client. Neither banned form ('NCAIF', 'DCCE') appears anywhere in the draft.

source_fidelity.evidence: All three required_concepts and all four inclusions are verifiably present: IPCC risk-chain terminal-point framing (line 3), the 11/260 draft-catalog anchor (line 3, traced via 01a row 2 to the chapter-2.4 evidence sidecar and its verified data_catalog_v4.csv figures), the two dimensions with contract-verbatim examples (lines 9-10), and the short MVD-structuring forward link (line 12). One caveat weighed and logged as finding F1: per 01a row 4 / 'Explicit gaps', the slow-onset example list (sea-level rise, shifting mean temperature, extreme heat/cold spells) is generic climate-science framing, not traced to a CRDB-specific project document. Verdict remains pass because this exact example list is contract-mandated verbatim (see writing-contract.json inclusions[3] and target_altitude), was approved by Boss at contract sign-off, and the sourcing gap is transparently disclosed in the sidecar rather than fabricated or concealed -- it is a minor, honestly-flagged caveat, not a source-fidelity failure of this draft's execution.

form_readability.evidence: Structure matches required_structures exactly: two-to-three continuous paragraphs (line 3 opening; the lines 7-10 dimension-establishing paragraph broken into the contract-permitted short list; line 12 closing) with no bold section subheadings breaking up the prose. The bold text at lines 9-10 ('**ลักษณะการเกิดผลกระทบ**', '**ลักษณะของมูลค่าความเสียหาย**') is a label inside the contract-permitted enumerated list, not a section subheading, consistent with the style pack's 'Structured Breakdowns for Complex Lists' rule. The IPCC risk-chain position is rendered as a figure placeholder (line 5), not inline arrows.

altitude.evidence: Stays at decision-maker depth throughout: no per-hazard or per-platform treatment, no quantitative valuation methodology for slow-onset damage (explicitly excluded by the contract and absent from the draft), no evidence tables. The DaLA-style damage/loss distinction (line 10) is a one-clause definition, not a valuation-methodology walkthrough.

headline_conclusion.evidence: The governing finding is stated directly and early (line 3): the country cannot measure whether assessed risk became real impact without L&D data, and the existing catalog has reserved the domain but not yet operationalized it. A reader gets this without reconstructing it from a list of project activities.

findings_over_process.evidence: The draft centers national/institutional stakes -- measurability of risk materialization, the catalog's domain gap, and the two-dimension structural axis for the coming MVD -- rather than describing how the consultant worked. The two consultant references (line 3, line 12) are single-clause attributions, not process narration.
